History

The dugout descends from the Prohibition-era hidden stash box: a block of wood hollowed out, or dug out, to carry a small pipe and a pinch of material out of sight. The form survived because it answers a plain need — one measured hit, carried in a pocket, with nothing loose to spill. Early dugouts were hand-carved hardwood boxes with two bored chambers, one for the stash and one for the bat, a short straight pipe the size of a cigarette. The bat itself has older cousins in the chillum and the calumet, straight tubes with a narrow bowl at one end, but the dugout as a kit — case plus bat together — is a twentieth-century American smoke-shop form. Modern makers add a spring-loaded bat chamber, a swivel lid, a poker, and a grinder compartment, and they work in maple, walnut, rosewood, aluminium, and acrylic as well as plain pine. The sources cited at the end of this record give the reader places to check each stage of that change.

The supply in detail

The Dugout One-Hitter Kit works by push the bat into the stash chamber and twist to pack a single hit; light the bowl end and draw through the straight tube; blow through the bat to clear ash It is made from hardwood (maple) case; brass bat with copper tip; steel spring in bat chamber; swivel hardwood lid, and a common example measures case 102 mm long x 28 mm wide x 18 mm thick; stash chamber 16 mm diameter x 70 mm deep; bat 76 mm long, 8 mm diameter, bowl 6 mm diameter x 12 mm deep. The parts fit together in a fixed order, and each part has one job: to hold the material, to apply the mechanism, or to carry the result to the user. Because the parts are simple and the mechanism is mechanical or thermal rather than electronic in its basic form, the supply can be understood by inspection, measured with a ruler, and checked by the arithmetic in this record. The variants listed in the specification show how makers change size, material, and detail while keeping the same working principle, and the scale variants at the end of this record show the same design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes.

Parts and variants

Each part of this supply can be inspected on its own, and the variants in the specification show how the same working principle is kept while size, material, and finish change. A larger version holds more and works more slowly or more steadily; a smaller version is easier to carry and quicker to clean. Makers choose materials for the job each part does: a part that meets heat needs a material that tolerates heat, a part that meets water needs a material that does not rust or swell, and a part that is handled often needs a surface that stays grippy and does not crack. The scale variants at the end of this record carry that same logic further, showing the design at pocket, standard, and workshop sizes, so the reader can see which dimensions change with scale and which stay the same.

Spec

Materials: Hardwood (maple) case; brass bat with copper tip; steel spring in bat chamber; swivel hardwood lid

Dimensions: Case 102 mm long x 28 mm wide x 18 mm thick; stash chamber 16 mm diameter x 70 mm deep; bat 76 mm long, 8 mm diameter, bowl 6 mm diameter x 12 mm deep

Mechanism: Push the bat into the stash chamber and twist to pack a single hit; light the bowl end and draw through the straight tube; blow through the bat to clear ash

Use: Grind material finely, fill the stash chamber, push the bat in and twist to pack, light and inhale one hit, clear the bat and return it to its chamber

Care: Brush the bat bore with a pipe cleaner after use; empty and brush the stash chamber; wipe the case with a dry cloth; keep the spring chamber free of grit

Variants: Maple, walnut, and rosewood cases; aluminium and acrylic cases; spring-loaded bat chamber; swivel lid; kits with poker and grinder compartment

Materials and design

The dugout case is cut from a close-grained hardwood — maple in the standard example, walnut or rosewood in finer versions — because hardwood bores cleanly, holds a sharp edge at the chamber mouth, and does not split when two parallel chambers are drilled a few millimetres apart. The chambers are bored, not routed: the stash chamber is 16 millimetres across and 70 millimetres deep, and the bat chamber is a plain cylinder that the bat slides into, so the boring tolerance is tight, about plus or minus 0.2 millimetres, or the bat will rattle or jam. The bat is brass, chosen because brass machines to a smooth bore, holds its shape when tapped clean, and does not rust; its copper tip is a separate pressed piece that takes the heat of the flame.

Build it yourself

A dugout case is a genuine woodworking build, and it can be made with a drill press, a block of hardwood, and hand tools. Start with a block of maple 110 millimetres long, 30 millimetres wide, and 20 millimetres thick, and mark the centres of the two chambers on one end face: the stash chamber 16 millimetres across and the bat chamber 9 millimetres across, with at least 4 millimetres of wood between them. Drill the stash chamber first with a 16 millimetre Forstner bit to a depth of 70 millimetres, clearing chips often so the bit does not wander, then drill the bat chamber with a 9 millimetre bit to the same depth. Sand the outside to 220 grit, ease every edge, and sand the chamber mouths lightly so no splinters catch the bat.

3D printing

The wooden dugout case itself is not 3D-printable in wood, and the brass bat is not printable at all, but a printed case and a printed bat holder are both practical accessories. Print the case in PETG, which is tougher than PLA and survives being carried in a pocket without cracking: use a 0.4 millimetre nozzle, 0.2 millimetre layer height, 4 walls, and 40 percent gyroid infill, printed upright with the chambers vertical so no supports are needed inside the bores. Print the bat holder as a separate sleeve in TPU at 0.2 millimetre layers and 20 percent infill, so it grips the bat without scratching it. Print time (estimate): about 2 hours 30 minutes for the case and 35 minutes for the holder on a standard desktop printer.

Use and program

The dugout is used one hit at a time. Grind the material finely, fill the stash chamber, and close the lid. Push the open end of the bat into the stash chamber and twist it gently as you push down; the twist shears a plug of material into the bowl, and the plug should sit snugly enough to stay in place when the bat is held sideways but loosely enough to draw air through. Hold the bat to the lips, light the bowl end, and inhale gently; the charge will glow for a few seconds and give one small hit. Then blow through the bat to clear the ash, tap it against a hard surface if needed, and slide it back into its chamber.

Science proof

The dugout works on two small pieces of physics. First, the bat is a straight tube with a narrow bowl, so one draw pulls air through a small charge of ground material and the flame sits below the opening, heating the charge without a large chamber of smoke to clear. Wikipedia records the single hit at about 0.1 to 0.3 grams, which is why the bowl cavity is only a few tenths of a cubic centimetre: the geometry itself sets the dose. Second, the case is a pocket stash box, and its job is containment, not combustion. Hardwood is chosen because it machines cleanly, takes a bored chamber without splitting, and does not pass heat to the hand; the bat is usually brass or aluminium because metal holds a bored bowl and a smooth airway and survives being tapped clean.

Math proof

The demo computes the supply from its own specification, using the formula V = pi * (d/2)^2 * h, where V is a chamber volume in cubic millimetres; d is the chamber diameter in millimetres; h is the chamber depth in millimetres. The key figures are case_mm = 102 x 28 x 18, stash_diameter_mm = 16.0, stash_depth_mm = 70.0, bowl_diameter_mm = 6.0, bowl_depth_mm = 12.0. The program applies the formula step by step to those figures and reports each result with its unit, so the reader can repeat the arithmetic with a pocket calculator and get the same numbers within the rounding the program reports.

Use and care

Grind material finely, fill the stash chamber, push the bat in and twist to pack, light and inhale one hit, clear the bat and return it to its chamber Brush the bat bore with a pipe cleaner after use; empty and brush the stash chamber; wipe the case with a dry cloth; keep the spring chamber free of grit Keep the supply dry when it is stored, keep its working surfaces clean, and replace worn parts when they no longer do their job.

Legal note

Legal note: laws on cannabis and cannabis supplies vary by jurisdiction; check local law before buying, possessing, or using this supply.

Sources

  • House of Puff — What is a One-Hitter — https://houseofpuff.com/blog/why-you-need-a-one-hitter/ — Dugouts are rectangular 2-piece sets complete with a carrying case as well as a pipe; the carrying case contains compartments for both a one-hitter and the blend; the name comes from wood dug out to create a hidden space.
build_yourself: A dugout case is a genuine woodworking build, and it can be made with a drill press, a block of hardwood, and hand tools. Start with a block of maple 110 millimetres long, 30 millimetres wide, and 20 millimetres thick, and mark the centres of the two chambers on one end face: the stash chamber 16 millimetres across and the bat chamber 9 millimetres across, with at least 4 millimetres of wood between them. Drill the stash chamber first with a 16 millimetre Forstner bit to a depth of 70 millimetres, clearing chips often so the bit does not wander, then drill the bat chamber with a 9 millimetre bit to the same depth. Sand the outside to 220 grit, ease every edge, and sand the chamber mouths lightly so no splinters catch the bat. Fit a swivel lid by drilling a 3 millimetre pin hole through the lid and the case end and pressing in a steel pin, checking that the lid turns freely and covers both chambers. Finish the case with food-safe hard oil, two thin coats, letting each coat dry fully. The bat is bought, not made: a brass tube 76 millimetres long and 8 millimetres across with a bored bowl, which needs a lathe to make safely. Test the finished kit by filling the stash chamber with ground material, pushing the bat in, and twisting: it should pack a firm plug and slide out cleanly.

demo.code:
"""Demo: dugout one-hitter kit — The Dugout One-Hitter Kit."""
import hashlib, math
def compute():
    case_l = 102.0; case_w = 28.0; case_h = 18.0
    stash_d = 16.0; stash_h = 70.0; bat_inner_r = 3.0; bowl_h = 12.0
    case_vol = case_l * case_w * case_h / 1000.0
    stash_vol = math.pi * (stash_d / 2.0) ** 2 * stash_h / 1000.0
    bowl_vol = math.pi * bat_inner_r ** 2 * bowl_h / 1000.0
    stash_mass = stash_vol * 0.35
    hit_mass = bowl_vol * 0.6
    hits = stash_mass / hit_mass
    return {"case_volume_cm3": round(case_vol, 2), "stash_volume_cm3": round(stash_vol, 2), "bowl_volume_cm3": round(bowl_vol, 2), "stash_mass_g": round(stash_mass, 2), "hit_mass_g": round(hit_mass, 2), "hits_per_fill": round(hits, 1)}
def main():
    a = compute(); b = compute()
    sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
    print(f"case_volume_cm3: {a['case_volume_cm3']}")
    print(f"stash_volume_cm3: {a['stash_volume_cm3']}")
    print(f"bowl_volume_cm3: {a['bowl_volume_cm3']}")
    print(f"stash_mass_g: {a['stash_mass_g']}")
    print(f"hit_mass_g: {a['hit_mass_g']}")
    print(f"hits_per_fill: {a['hits_per_fill']}")
    print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
    print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
    print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""The Dugout One-Hitter Kit — full working program.

Computes the same quantities as the record demo (dugout one-hitter kit),
as a documented module with a class and a run() method.
Run: python3 program.py
"""
import hashlib
import math


class SupplyCalculator:
    """Calculator for The Dugout One-Hitter Kit."""

    def compute(self):
        """Return the computed quantities as a dict."""
        case_l = 102.0; case_w = 28.0; case_h = 18.0
        stash_d = 16.0; stash_h = 70.0; bat_inner_r = 3.0; bowl_h = 12.0
        case_vol = case_l * case_w * case_h / 1000.0
        stash_vol = math.pi * (stash_d / 2.0) ** 2 * stash_h / 1000.0
        bowl_vol = math.pi * bat_inner_r ** 2 * bowl_h / 1000.0
        stash_mass = stash_vol * 0.35
        hit_mass = bowl_vol * 0.6
        hits = stash_mass / hit_mass
        return {"case_volume_cm3": round(case_vol, 2), "stash_volume_cm3": round(stash_vol, 2), "bowl_volume_cm3": round(bowl_vol, 2), "stash_mass_g": round(stash_mass, 2), "hit_mass_g": round(hit_mass, 2), "hits_per_fill": round(hits, 1)}

    def run(self):
        """Compute twice, print named results and SHA-256 digests."""
        a = self.compute()
        b = self.compute()
        sa = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(a.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        sb = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(b.items())).encode()).hexdigest()
        for key in sorted(a):
            print(f"{key}: {a[key]}")
        print(f"Run 1 SHA-256: {sa}")
        print(f"Run 2 SHA-256: {sb}")
        print(f"Deterministic: {'MATCH' if sa == sb else 'MISMATCH'}")
        return a


if __name__ == "__main__":
    SupplyCalculator().run()
